LESSON: ADDING VALUE TO CROP PRODUCE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Production Techniques
Topic 4.3: Adding Value to Crop Produce
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Adding Value to Crop Produce, part of Production Techniques in Grade 7 AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we add value to crop produce? How can we add value to crop produce?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Adding Value to Crop Produce together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Integrity: applying laid down procedures when learners ethically process crop produce to add value.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Food and nutrition security as learners process crop produce for value addition.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learners relate the value addition concept to commodity marketing learnt in Pre-Technical Studies.

Learners are guided to:

• discuss ways of adding value to crop produce

such as potatoes, cassava, groundnuts, simsim,

sweet potatoes, and pumpkin.

• process a provided sample of crop produce

such as potatoes, cassava, groundnuts, simsim,

sweet potatoes and pumpkin to add value using

appropriate methods like drying and frying.

• compare the processed crop produce to raw

crop produce in terms of monetary value and

storage life to appreciate the importance of

value addition.
